doc.title: Basic Types of TJS2
doc.para:
Primitive Types There are several primitive types defined in tjsTypes.h.
tjs_int Signed integer (at least 32-bit)
tjs_uint Unsigned integer (at least 32-bit)
tjs_int8 8-bit signed integer
tjs_uint8 8-bit unsigned integer
tjs_int16 16-bit signed integer
tjs_uint16 16-bit unsigned integer
tjs_int32 32-bit signed integer
tjs_uint32 32-bit unsigned integer
tjs_int64 64-bit signed integer
tjs_uint64 64-bit unsigned integer
tjs_char Wide character (used as a primitive type for string types in TJS2)
tjs_nchar Narrow character
tjs_real Real number type (double)
tTVInteger Same as tjs_int64
tTVReal Same as tjs_real

tTJSString The tTJSString type is a string type used in TJS2 that handles zero-terminated tjs_char strings. It is defined in tjsString.cpp / tjsString.h. It can also be used via the shorter type name ttstr. In addition to automatically managing memory for strings, this type has high compatibility with .

eTJS The eTJS type is the base type for C++ exception objects. It is defined in tjsError.h. It has a method called GetMessage, which allows you to retrieve the message string thrown with the exception.

TJS_W A macro for converting string literals to the tjs_char * type.
Example : TJS_W("string literal")
